title: Are You Ready to Run? How to Campaign for Woodstock City Council

location.venue: Zoom link will be sent to registered attendees shortly before the event.

description:
Our city deserves leadership that listens, leads with integrity, and reflects the people who actually live here. That means we need non-MAGA candidates to run—and win—in Woodstock’s upcoming City Council races for Wards 1 and 3.

If you're fed up with unopposed extremists controlling local government, it's time to change the game. This training will show you exactly how to do that—whether you want to run yourself or help someone else step up.

We’ll cover:

- What the job actually involves and why it matters

- What kind of support you can expect—and what you’ll need to bring to the table

You don’t need to be a political insider. You don’t need to know everything. You just need the courage to show up—and a community that’s ready to fight for a better future.

Let’s take back our city from MAGA extremism. Let’s build something better.

description:
Join us for Roadmap to Winning, a powerful gathering to celebrate how we beat back MAGA extremism—not with more money, but with more heart, more truth, and the will of the people. 

This event is more than a victory lap—it’s a strategy session for the future. We turned the tide in 2025. Now, we build the momentum to turn this first blue wave into a tidal wave in 2026. Learn from the organizers, leaders, and everyday heroes who made it happen—and how we do it again, bigger and bolder.

Together, we map the road ahead. Let’s keep fighting. Let’s keep winning.

**Featured Guest: Adam Kinzinger**

Adam Kinzinger is a former Republican congressman from Illinois and U.S. Air Force veteran known for his outspoken opposition to MAGA extremism. A key member of the January 6th Committee, he prioritized truth and accountability over party loyalty. After leaving Congress, he founded Country First to promote democracy and combat political division.

**Dr. John Biggan: HEB ISD Trustee**

Dr. John Biggan is a cognitive neuroscientist and data scientist who works in the child welfare system, using research and data to improve the lives of the children in this community, the state, and nationwide. A longtime Hurst resident and advocate for public education, he brings a research-driven approach to his role on the HEB ISD Board of Trustees, focusing on student success, teacher support, and fiscal responsibility.

Vanessa Pacheco, single-member district 2; elected in June 2022. Mrs. Pacheco is the Chief Operations Officer for Carrolton Injury Law. She and her husband, Jorge, have a daughter who graduated from Berkner High School in 2020 and a son who graduated from Richardson High School in 2023.

Omar was elected to the Richardson City Council, Place 7 in May 2009, defeating incumbent Dennis Stewart by 51.54% to 48.46%. On May 3, 2025, Omar defeated incumbent Bob Dubey 54.4% to 41.6% in the mayoral race.

**Laney Hawes: Texas Freedom to Read Project and, Keller ISD Families for Public Education; Co-Founder**

She's passionate about true grassroots activism, public education, and the freedom to read. Laney resides in North Fort Worth with her husband and four children.

They’ve replaced the symbol of nearly 250 years of struggle, sacrifice, and aspiration with the name of a convicted felon. They’ve chosen a cult of personality over the principles of a nation. Let them keep their blue Trump flags. Let them wave them at their rallies with their silly red hats, plaster them on their trucks, and fly them in their yards. That’s not our flag. Fly it in the face of an administration that thrives on division, lies, and the erosion of the very liberties we hold dear. Fly it as a hat tip to the generations who laid down their lives so we could protest, vote, and speak freely today. Fly it for the millions who’ve marched, bled, and died to protect this nation from the kind of tyranny we now face at home.

This isn’t about nostalgia or blind allegiance. It’s about defiance. We’ll take back the red, white, and blue. We’ll fly it as a symbol of resistance, of resilience, of a patriotism that doesn’t divide but unites. We’ll fly it for the America we believe in—an America that belongs to all of us, not just the loudest or the most hateful. And when we do, we’ll show the world that the soul of this nation isn’t found in one man or one party. It’s found in us, in our defiance, in our hope, and in the flag we raise together. title: Knock doors with Swing Left East Bay
description:
Canvassing has been shown time and again to be the most effective way to engage with voters. Canvassing early shows the community that we’re not waiting until right before the election to reach out. 

​​Join us to talk to Democratic voters California’s 13th Congressional District, a seat flipped in 2024 by Democrat Adam Gray by just 187 votes. Talking to Democrats now will ensure that we can hold this seat as we take back the House majority in 2026!

Arrival time is 9:30 am to pick up supplies, get assigned turf, and get trained. Then we will head out to knock doors, focusing on learning what issues are most pressing for voters, sharing about Adam Gray’s accomplishments and identifying new volunteers.

If you need a ride, we have carpools available. The exact location will be provided at least one week prior to the canvass date. If you want to drive, please let us know. Just bring your smartphone or tablet and a charger, some water, sunscreen, comfortable shoes, and a smile.​

Don’t worry if you’ve never done this before–we’ll cover everything you need to know. And once you get going, you'll find that talking to voters is fun and rewarding.

title: NO KINGS! Voices for Justice-Lake Forest Park

location.venue: Town Center - intersection of Bothell Way NE & Ballinger

description:
VOICES FOR JUSTICE-LAKE FOREST PARK joins the NO KINGS! national day of action and mass mobilization in response to increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption from Trump and his allies.
 
PLEASE BRING SHELF-STABLE FOOD DONATIONS for Hopelink Food Bank if you are able.
 
We’ve watched as they’ve cracked down on free speech, detained people for their political views, deported refugees and immigrants and American citizens, defied the courts, undermined clean energy and environmental protection, and devastated funding for research, education, health care and food security. They’ve done this all while continuing to serve and enrich their billionaire allies.
 
We the people say no thrones, no crowns, no kings.
 
A core principle behind our events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

Share photos/videos with #NoKings or the organizer for this event — please DO NOT PHOTOGRAPH CHILDREN without their families’ consent, and when possible ask people in close-up photos if they are OK being photographed. Some will prefer to hold up just their signs to be photographed and shared.

ACCESSIBILITY NOTES:  Several buses come to this corner including 372, 522 and 331. There is an accessible parking lot and a grassy lawn area for people who would like space for chairs, walkers or for children to participate and play. This is a family friendly event! Bothell Way and Ballinger Way are major roads. We’ll mark a border along the edge of the sidewalk with chalk as a reminder to step back. There are accessible public restrooms available in the Lake Forest Park Town Center.
 
A FEW ADDITIONAL WAYS TO TAKE ACTION NOW:
 
Join Lake Forest Park for Peace every Saturday from 11:00-noon at this same corner for their weekly vigil for peace and justice. This group has been demonstrating every week since December 2002. Join them!
 
Register to vote and be sure your friends and family are registered: Washington online voter registration: https://vote.gov/register/washington. (For registration outside of Washington state: https://www.usa.gov/voter-registration)
 
Call your Members of Congress — thank them, urge them, make demands, let them know you’re paying attention. 5Calls.org and https://indivisible.org/ provide contact and background information on issues.

Share the Know Your Rights for Immigrants website and app information.  The app is available in many languages and includes a function to quickly contact all emergency contacts if an ICE event is imminent: https://nakasec.org/resources/know-your-rights/
 
Voices for Justice Lake Forest Park, will continue to host demonstrations and other actions — look for us via mobilize.us, indivisible.org, in Shoreline Area News and in local social media.

title: Protest @ Tesla Lyndhurst, Thursday, May 29th, 12:00 to 2:00 PM
description:

title: Write Postcards to Register Voters
description:
Join us at New Parkway Theater to write postcards to register people to vote in New Jersey, Pennsylvania and California. We will be using addresses and scripts from Field Team 6, which focuses on registering to vote Democrats is purple States and districts. 
Registering people to vote is an activity that will benefit us at any time and not just near mid terms. This is long term action that will bear fruit down the road
We have a capacity of 15 people for this event. 

What Do I Need To Do ?
Bring yourself, a pen (we will have some pens), and come up to the mezzanine level on the New Parkway, you'll see us there 

We will give you a script, addresses and 20 postcards. 
You will need to bring stamps or you can get them from us. 20 postcard stamps ($0.55) for $11.00
The New Parkway serves good food including pizza, burgers, shakes and more. 

Registering people to vote is how we win the midterms.
